questions.question: Is a hotel 'residential' for the building-control open-space minimum and the clause 52 affordable-housing bonus?

readings.reading: No. Reg 55 clause 1 names hotels as public buildings, and clause 33 (2) gives public buildings 10 in 100.

$cite.token: โรงแรม
$cite.clause: ข้อ 1 อาคารสาธารณะ

$cite.token: อาคารสาธารณะ

readings.reading: Yes. Reg 55 clause 1 defines a residential building as one lived in day and night, permanently or temporarily, and clause 33 (2) sends a building also used as a residence to the 30 in 100 rule.

$cite.token: อาศัยอย่างถาวรหรือชั่วคราว
$cite.clause: ข้อ 1 อาคารอยู่อาศัย

$cite.token: ใช้เป็นที่อยู่อาศัย

questions.why: Feasibility should under-promise: the 30 in 100 reading gives the smaller footprint, and the clause 33 (2) proviso reads as written for buildings people sleep in.

questions.question: Is a condo a public building, so that the clause 53 public-open-space bonus and the clause 54 public-parking bonus can apply?

readings.reading: No. Reg 55 clause 1 defines a public building as a building for public gathering, and clause 33 treats multi-unit residential buildings as their own class.

$cite.token: ชุมนุมคน
$cite.clause: ข้อ 1 อาคารสาธารณะ

$cite.token: อาคารอยู่อาศัยรวม

readings.reading: Yes. The list of examples ends with 'and so on', so it is open, and the plan only says 'public building under the building control law'.

$cite.token: เป็นต้น
$cite.clause: ข้อ 1 อาคารสาธารณะ

$cite.token: อาคารสาธารณะ

questions.why: Every listed example is a place where the public gathers; private homes are not, so a condo should get no clause 53 or clause 54 bonus.

questions.question: Is an office a public building for the clause 53 and clause 54 FAR bonuses?

readings.reading: No. Reg 55 defines offices separately and the public-building examples never name an office.

$cite.token: สำนักงาน
$cite.clause: ข้อ 1 สำนักงาน

$cite.token: ห้างสรรพสินค้า

readings.reading: Yes. The definition covers gathering for commerce, which a large office arguably serves.

$cite.token: การพาณิชยกรรม
$cite.clause: ข้อ 1 อาคารสาธารณะ

questions.why: Offices have their own definition; reading them into the public-building list would also change their fire and open-space class.

questions.question: Which building-control open-space minimum does the plan's 'not below the building control minimum' point to?

readings.reading: Apply Reg 55 clause 33 (share of the largest floor), the Bangkok bylaw clause 52 (share of land) and, for high-rise or extra-large buildings, Reg 33 clause 6 (share of land); the largest required area governs.

พื้นที่ที่ดิน
พื้นที่ดินที่ใช้เป็นที่ตั้งอาคาร

readings.reading: Apply Reg 55 clause 33 to ordinary buildings and Reg 33 clause 6 to high-rise; the bylaw's share of land is ignored where it differs, because a local bylaw cannot conflict with a ministerial regulation.

$cite.token: ร้อยละ 30

questions.why: A Bangkok permit office checks both the ministerial regulation and the bylaw; meeting the largest requirement satisfies every reading.

questions.question: Which parking rule governs a plot in this zone?

readings.reading: The Bangkok bylaw clauses 83 to 85 (hotel by rooms, condo 1 per unit of 60 m² or more, office 1 per 60 m²).

$cite.token: ข้อ 83

readings.reading: Reg 7 clause 3 (1), which applies only inside the old Bangkok metropolitan municipality area (hotel by lobby and commercial area).

$cite.token: เฉพาะในเขตเทศบาลนครหลวง

readings.reading: Compute both and require the higher count for each building type.

$cite.token: มากกว่าเป็นเกณฑ์

questions.why: The two texts agree on condo and office and differ only for hotels; taking the higher count is safe and needs no map of the 1971 municipal boundary.

questions.question: The permeable 50% is a share of which open space?

readings.reading: Of the minimum open space the plan requires (4.5% of total floor area).

$cite.token: ร้อยละสี่จุดห้า
$cite.clause: ข้อ 16 วรรคสาม (2)

readings.reading: Of all open space actually left on the plot.

$cite.token: ของพื้นที่ว่าง
$cite.clause: ข้อ 16 วรรคสาม (2)

questions.why: The sentence sits inside the OSR rule and 'open space' refers back to the open space that rule requires; the other reading would penalise leaving extra open space.

questions.question: Does parking floor area count in the total building floor area for FAR and OSR?

readings.reading: Yes. The definition counts every storey of every building, and clause 54 has to exempt bonus public parking explicitly, which implies ordinary parking counts.

$cite.token: อัตราส่วนพื้นที่อาคารรวมทุกชั้น
ยกเว้นไม่ต้องนำมาพิจารณา
$cite.clause: ข้อ 54 วรรคสอง

readings.reading: No. Parking is not floor area people occupy, so it is left out of total floor area.

$cite.token: พื้นที่อาคาร
$cite.clause: ข้อ 1 พื้นที่อาคาร

questions.why: The plan defines its own term with no exclusion, and the explicit clause 54 exemption only makes sense if parking otherwise counts.

questions.question: For this zone's office limit (operating area above 10,000 m² needs a 16 m road or a station within 500 m), is operating area the office's total floor area?

readings.reading: Yes. Clause 4 defines operating area to include areas in continuous use for the business, inside or outside the building.

ต่อเนื่อง

readings.reading: No. Count only rentable office space; lobbies, plant and parking are not 'operating' the business.

$cite.token: สำนักงาน
$cite.clause: ข้อ 16 วรรคสอง (10)

questions.why: The definition reaches beyond the building itself; using total floor area can only make the tool stricter.

questions.question: When a hotel or office relies on the road-width exemption, what must the tool check under clause 36 (as corrected on 9 Oct 2013)?

readings.reading: Enforce the right-of-way tier and the minimum frontage on that road; show the continuity, connecting-road width and distance tests as a manual check, because they depend on the road network beyond the plot.

$cite.token: ขนาดเขตทาง
$cite.clause: ข้อ 16 วรรคสอง (8)

questions.why: Frontage is visible on the drawn plot, so skipping it would let a 4 m wide flag lot pass; the network tests cannot be read from one plot.

questions.question: Does the 13 Mar 2026 Bangkok bylaw change anything in clause 16, this zone's clause, that this pack uses?

readings.reading: No value this pack uses changes. Of the bylaw's 21 articles, article 10 rewrites item (1), the factory item, of clause 16, this zone's prohibited uses (factories of up to 500 m² stay allowed and the annex's factory type 90, water-supply works, is added), and article 19 adds a new clause 33/1 that takes state medical and public-health land use out of the land-use rules of clauses 8 to 32. FAR, open space, and the hotel and office conditions are not touched. So the amendment is not factory-only, but its other change does not reach private condominiums, offices or hotels.

$cite.clause: ข้อ 10 (amends plan ข้อ 16 วรรคสอง (1))

$cite.clause: บัญชีท้ายข้อบัญญัติ ลำดับที่ 90

readings.reading: Treat the amendment as unread: mark every value for this zone as unverified against it.

$cite.token: ตอนพิเศษ ๖๖ ง

questions.why: The gazette's 6 pages were rendered at 300 dpi (PyMuPDF 1.27.2.3) and read with Tesseract OCR (tesseract.js 7.0.0, Thai data) on 20 Nov 2026, then every line was checked against the page images, because the OCR misreads Thai numerals. Articles 3 to 18 each replace the factory item of one zone's prohibited uses, article 19 adds clause 33/1, and articles 20 and 21 add factory type 90 to the plan's annex and replace its type 76 (1) with the bylaw's annex. Nothing else is amended.

questions.question: Does a building on a public road need the bylaw clause 52 (6) front open space (6 m, or 12 m above 3 storeys)?

readings.reading: No, if it meets clause 53: the road-facing building line is longer than 1/8 of the perimeter and within 20 m of the road.

$cite.token: แนวอาคารด้านที่ประชิดติดริมทางสาธารณะ
